canonical.behaviour:
Two new review rules. Each is written in one place, with short pointers from the skills that use it.

Read the output first. When reviewed work produces something a person reads (message, report, dashboard, document), a fresh reviewer first gets only the finished output and who reads it, without the plan. It says which question each part answers and names the obvious questions left out. Only then do the plan and code reviews start. Today such a question would be filed as a note that nobody acts on. With this rule you get it as a question before delivery, unless the agreed plan excludes it in words. The rule stands in AUDIT.md. Code review, plan review, spar and delivery point to it.

Open the source. A source named for a method, formula, number or standard carries its URL and the exact sentence or formula that was read. Otherwise it says unverified, with the reason. This holds for question cards and offers too, and is checked before they are sent. Reviewers open each source themselves. The rule stands in WRITING.md. The old source rule (Unslop 5) asked only for a source name, so a wrong or unread source passed, and reviewers could report a breach only as a note. It becomes a pointer, not a second copy.

You can reject these choices. There is one extra reader per finished output, not per ticket. Agent instructions and simple rewording are left out. With no finished output yet, a plan review reads a sample, or says that nothing could be checked. In spar, the reader is an evidence helper and does not use up a debater launch. There is no automatic check, because a script cannot tell which sentence relies on a source. Two short source lines stay in the spar briefs, because debaters load no files.
exclusions: commit, push, release, version bump, changelog and installing the change
conditions: at most 4 subagent test runs on made-up material, plus one reviewer and its repair check
in tests/test_spar.py only the size limits change, by at most 60 words each for spar/SKILL.md and T3.md
no client, project or event name in any changed file
checks: full test suite and tools/validate.py, compared with the result before the change
new text tests fail before the change and pass after it
one independent review, including one place per rule
test runs with the old and the new text: the reviewer names a missing earlier-period comparison, and a reviewer catches a wrong cited section
